# Quick start

## Install

**From a wheel** (Linux x86-64 and aarch64): download the `.whl` from a
[GitHub release](https://github.com/aclater/pysacd/releases), then

```sh
pip install 'pysacd-*.whl[convert]'   # engine and libFLAC included; [convert] adds mutagen for tagging
pysacd --version                      # shows how the engine was built
```

Wheels are portable builds: the PCM filters pick AVX-512, AVX2 or the baseline
when the library loads.

**From source** (needs gcc and make; `flac-devel` for FLAC output):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/aclater/pysacd && cd pysacd
pip install -e '.[convert]'                  # builds a portable engine
make                                         # optional: rebuild it for this CPU (-march=native)
```

`PYSACD_NATIVE=1 pip install .` builds for this CPU from the start. Linux only
for now; Windows and macOS are tracked in #8.

## Read a disc's TOC

From a file, or from a PS3:

```console
$ pysacd toc album.iso
== album.iso
Disc:      Nick Drake - Nick Drake: A Treasury
  version 1.20  hybrid=True  set 1/1  date 2004-08-21
Area TWOCHTOC: Stereo, DST, 15 tracks, 52:17:09 (LSN 624-453388)
   1. 01:29:68  Introduction - SACD Stereo [Nick Drake]
   ...
$ pysacd toc --json 192.0.2.10:2002 > disc.json
```

## Extract exactly as sacd_extract would

```console
$ pysacd-extract -2 -m -s -i album.iso       # DSF, stereo + multichannel
```

See [pysacd-extract](sacd_extract.md) for migrating and compatibility.

## Convert into your library

With your own naming and MusicBrainz tags:

```console
$ pysacd convert -f flac -o ~/Music album.iso
MusicBrainz: A Treasury — Nick Drake (2004, Hybrid SACD (SACD layer, 2 channels)) [barcode, ISRC 15/15]
Stereo DST: 15 tracks -> ~/Music/Nick Drake/A Treasury [SACD]
```

See [converting](converting.md) for templates and tags.

## Use it as a library

```python
from pysacd import SACDImage
from pysacd._native import OutputSpec, run_area

with SACDImage("album.iso") as img:
    area = img.read_toc().multichannel
    specs = [OutputSpec("flac", f"{t.number:02d}.flac", t.start.total_frames,
                        t.start.total_frames + t.duration.total_frames) for t in area.tracks]
    run_area(img, "album.iso", area, specs, pcm_rate=88200,
             progress=lambda p: print(f"{p.frames_done}/{p.frames_total}"))
```

To cancel, raise from the progress callback (Ctrl-C works too); the engine
stops cleanly. See [the Python library](library.md).
